monument_name: Vināyaka Pañcadevala Śikhara Temple 2 (built between the 13th and 15th cent.)
description_en: Vināyaka Pañcadevala Śikhara Temple 2, built between the 13th and 15th centuries, is situated on a large platform that houses four medievalśikharatemples and one more recent shrine. The complex is in Binayak (Vināyaka), one of the Achham district's main market towns.The Temple 2 faces north-east and lacks doorjambs and a lintel.Antarāla(skt.) projections frame the entrance to thesanctumon both sides of the door. Thesanctumis empty and has a very limited inner space that only allows for the deposit of offerings. It could have contained a smallśivaliṅga. The ceiling is made of two uncarved stone slabs.The complex of these four temples in Binayak is known as Pañcadevala, which translates as 'five temples'. This emic designation is typically applied to groups of more than two temples, even if when there are more or fewer than five temples. However, Pañcadeval is also a term for five temples built on a quincunx plan, also referred to aspañcāyatana(skt. 'Five altars'). The Pañcadevala plan is mostly found in the districts of Dailekh, Achham and Kalikot, which corresponds to the Rāskoṭi kings' domain (Andolfatto 2019 and Andolfatto 2022). This dynasty ruled from the late fourteenth century to the late eighteenth century.The group of Binayak Pañcadevala has often been considered as a Pañcadevala, without regard for the actual plan. According to Dilli Raj Sharma, '[...] the temples of Vināyak are built to serve the idea of the pañcha dewal style. However, the structural elements do not fit the plan of five temples' (Sharma 2012, p. 228).  Indeed, the site only has fourśikharatemples and, according to the general plan. However, it is unlikely that it was ever built as a Pañcadevala group. The Temple ACH0072 contains an inscription from ŚS 1202 (1280 CE). A temple of comparable size is constructed north-west of the Temple ACH0072. These two temples were most likely constructed at the same time.The two smallerśikharatemples are oriented in a way that has not been seen on any known Pañcadevala of the Karnali basin. Unless we are in presence of an uncomplete and new type of Pañcadevala, theśikharasACH0070 and ACH0071 must be later additions, dating from the late 13th century to the 15th century.The monuments of Binayak are described by Prayag Sharma (Sharma 1972) and the ŚS 1202 inscription of ACH0072 is discussed by Mahes Raj Pant (Pant 2009).
